\[
T_\sigma = \sigma^2 \max(\lambda_{\max}, 0),
\qquad
R(x) = \max_\sigma T_\sigma(x)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\lambda_{\max}\): The larger Hessian eigenvalue
- \(\sigma\): The scale

The Hessian is the matrix of second derivatives of the image smoothed by a Gaussian of sigma. Across a dark line, the brightness bends up, so the larger eigenvalue lambda_max is positive. Sato's measure in 2D is that eigenvalue, clipped at 0. Second derivatives shrink as the Gaussian grows, so the factor sigma^2 makes the scales comparable, as in scale-space theory. The filter keeps the largest T over the scales and stretches the result so the strongest response is white.
